rationale.conceptual: The paper applies well-established DFT methods (PBE+D2, CI-NEB) to a battery anode problem; no novel algorithm, only a routine computational protocol.
rationale.execution: Reproducing requires geometry optimization, adsorption site scanning, CI-NEB diffusion barriers, incremental Li loading capacity determination, all with careful convergence; a multi-stage pipeline with many dependent calculations and fragile handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: Standard DFT study of anodes; conceptually simple but execution involves multi-step heavy DFT calculations.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small supercells (up to ~12 atoms) for plane-wave DFT; modest k-point sampling and no large datasets; memory per job is a few GB.
